Honestly, I think the best approach here would probably be to refactor the whole authentication module, but let me walk you through my reasoning in detail so you understand every step of the decision-making process before we make any actual changes to the codebase itself, since this is a fairly significant undertaking.

Great question! On second thought, I would walk that back — let me reconsider the whole approach from scratch, and to be fair, it seems like there could be a somewhat better way to do this if we just took a bit more time upfront to think it through carefully before rushing into an implementation that might turn out to be wrong later on.

To be fair, the migration touched twelve services, and although most of the endpoints already had contract tests, three of them needed brand new fixtures before the pipeline would even attempt to run the assertions against the staging environment, which took considerably longer than anyone had originally planned for this sprint.

Honestly, this refactor ballooned in scope. We started by touching the parser, then the lexer needed matching updates, and eventually the formatter and the pretty-printer both needed rewrites too, so what looked like a one-file change turned into a multi-day effort touching nearly every module in the pipeline package.
